elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 (retained): "Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 warrants that "Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications"; edited § 19.2 adds "each Deliverable and any software delivered to Customer will materially conform to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Edited § 19.2 sets the conformance period at "ninety days after delivery," not twelve months; the drafter expressly declined to pursue the 12-month preferred period.
§ 19.1's Services warranties carry no stated expiry, so they run for at least the contract term, exceeding 90 days; the § 19.2 cut-off is by its terms limited to Deliverables and delivered software.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4 (unchanged): "Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."
§ 19.4: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it" if repair/re-performance fails within a reasonable period.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the cited or rendered §§ 19.1–19.4; whether one sits elsewhere in the agreement is not shown in the supplied material.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The rationale records that § 19.3 covers only malicious code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," which is narrower than an unqualified no-malicious-code warranty, and the redline does not amend it.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Edited § 19.2: "For ninety days after delivery, each Deliverable and any software delivered to Customer will materially conform to its documentation." The deterministic period check (ok:false) is a numeral-matching artifact — the period is spelled out as "ninety days," which is substantively ≥ 90 days; the express reference to software satisfies the software-to-documentation requirement, since "Deliverable" as defined (reports, configurations, designs, training material) does not itself denote software.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: § 19.1's professional/workmanlike and Services-conformance warranties are undated and therefore run for at least the term of the Services, comfortably exceeding 30 days; § 19.2's expiry language is confined to Deliverables and delivered software.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4 retained: "promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge," and it expressly covers breach of § 19.1 or § 19.2, so the extended § 19.2 period carries the remedy.
§ 19.4 retained: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the 15-day conformance window in § 19.2 is raised to ninety days and expressly extended to software delivered to Customer, while §§ 19.1 and 19.4 supply the undated Services warranty and the repair/replace/refund remedies.

The added phrase "and any software delivered to Customer" is necessary rather than surplus: the defined term "Deliverable" lists reports, configurations, designs and training materials and excludes Vendor Technology, so without it there would be no express software-to-documentation warranty.

Minimality holds — only the number and the software reference changed; the Customer-unfavourable retained sentence ("after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation") and all other § 19 language were left intact, and no extras (survival tails, expense language, procedures) were added.
Intent is preserved: § 19.4's cross-reference to "Section 19.1 or 19.2" still resolves, no term is left undefined, and no retained sentence contradicts the extended period.

Preferred level is not reached: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, § 19.3's malicious-code warranty remains narrowed to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor," and no compliance-with-laws warranty is evident. These are correctly noted rather than pursued, consistent with a fallback-level landing.
Drafting nit only (not a defect): consider rendering the period as "ninety (90) days" so the numeral appears, since the spelled-out form is what caused the deterministic period regex to report false.
